patients.summary: Healthy graduate student who joined in 2021. A university postural research visit finds a brief orthostatic drop; later a 48-hour religious fast (glucose 68), a food-limited hiking trip with mild dehydration, and a post-10K collapse in the ED all come back to the same tendency to orthostatic lightheadedness. Otherwise routine young-adult preventive care.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Caller is a new grad student in the area, moved in early August, wants a primary doctor locally. Explained membership, he is fine with it. Insurance is the university student plan, member ID taken, card to be scanned at visit.
Booked new patient physical 9/14 9:00. Asked him to come fasting for labs. Sent records release for his prior primary care office to fill out on the portal.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and physical

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 yo man, first-year graduate student, moved to Easthampton last month for school. Establishing with us. No current concerns.

PMH: none. PSH: none.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: no heart disease, no fainting, no sudden deaths in the family as far as he knows.
SH: never smoked, does not drink, no drug use. Single, lives in an apartment in town.
Immunizations: says childhood vaccines are complete and he had both Pfizer doses this spring. Records release signed, we will pull the old chart.

ROS: negative across the board. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, mood good.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI normal. Thin, well appearing. HEENT clear, TMs normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement, no adenopathy. Heart regular rate, no murmurs. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no tenderness or organ enlargement. Skin without rashes. Neuro grossly nonfocal.

PHQ-9 1. AUDIT-C 0.

A/P: healthy young adult.
- Baseline labs today: CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screening, discussed and he agrees.
- Flu shot when the fall supply arrives, nurse visit.
- Tdap timing once the old records come in.
- Annual physical, can reach me by text or portal any time.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Vikram, everything from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar, and cholesterol. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were nonreactive, so those don't need repeating unless something changes. Have a good start to the semester.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Prior primary care and pediatric records, 2004 through 2021, 46 pages, received by secure fax and scanned.

Summary abstracted by MA:
- Well visits yearly through childhood and most college years. No chronic problems listed. No surgeries. No medications. NKDA.
- Last physical there 01/2020: normal exam, normal CBC and metabolic panel.
- Immunizations: MMR x2, varicella x2, MenACWY 2009 and 2014, HPV series x3 completed 2011, Tdap 06/2016. COVID Pfizer 4/19/21 and 5/10/21 per CDC card copy in the packet.
- Flu vaccines most years, not all dated.
Entered into immunization history. Original to scanned media.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu vaccine. Feels well today, no fever. No prior vaccine reactions, NKDA. Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, VIS reviewed. Tolerated well, waited 15 min without problems.

documents.title: Form for student insurance
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, the university insurance office wants a form signed saying I have a primary care provider for the coming year's enrollment. I uploaded it here. Is that something you can do? Thanks, Vikram

documents.title: RE: Form for student insurance
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Vikram, got it. Signed and faxed to the insurance office this morning, copy is in your documents tab.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Rescheduled from late August (schedule conflict on his end).
No new issues this year. Second year of the program, busy but fine. Sleeps 7 hrs. Eats regular meals. No meds. NKDA. Still no tobacco or alcohol.
ROS neg.
PE: vitals as charted, weight steady. Well. Oropharynx clear. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs CTA. Abd benign. Skin clear. No edema.
PHQ-2 0.
Plan: labs not needed this year, all normal last fall. Flu shot given today. Mentioned the new bivalent COVID booster, he will get it at the pharmacy near campus. RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Booster
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I got the bivalent Pfizer booster Saturday at the pharmacy on campus. Sore arm for a day and that was all.

documents.title: RE: Booster
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks, added to your immunization record with the 10/15 date.
